errors.quote: Calculate the time-derivative of the chemical output ($d[ATP]/dt$)
errors.issue: With luciferase in the reaction, net concentration change includes reporter consumption. A standard intensity curve does not convert this derivative to gross synthesis; calibrate loss/response dynamics or collect quenched reporter-free product.

errors.quote: Calibrate the rotational magnetic field to ensure the applied torque exceeds the theoretical energy required for ATP synthesis
errors.issue: Torque cannot directly be compared with energy. Integrate transmitted torque over angle, quantify dissipation and chemical free-energy demand; no operational actuator/torque calibration is supplied.

errors.quote: buffer containing saturating concentrations of ADP and Pi, entirely devoid of initial ATP.
errors.issue: Neither saturation nor complete ATP absence is established. The recipe omits magnesium qualification, measured contamination limits and the finite bound-ATP pool that could be released.

errors.quote: Repeat across $N = 50$ distinct single-molecule F1 preparations
errors.issue: The open shared reporter solution does not attribute ATP independently to each molecule. Define independent preparations/chambers, assay sensitivity and a hierarchy matched to chemical sampling.

errors.quote: we conclude that F1 coupling is irreversible or slips under reverse mechanical strain
errors.issue: Verified marker rotation plus a nonsignificant ATP result does not establish irreversibility. Adequate work transmission, sensitivity, chemistry and retained activity must be demonstrated; the proposed controls do not provide those bounds.

errors.quote: **C4 (No-Substrate Control):** Force reverse rotation in a buffer lacking ADP and Pi.
errors.issue: Both substrates are removed together, and there is no catalytically inactive F1 control. Separate substrate omissions and matched inactive/uncoupled controls are needed to distinguish phosphate-dependent synthesis from alternative chemistry.

rationale: Finds the correct next question and includes simultaneous angle and chemical recording with a sensible empirical sign. The plan is too underqualified for the requested discrimination: reporter flux, torque-energy units, chemical prerequisites and independent chemical units require substantial redesign. The negative inference is overly strong.
reference_guardrails: The packet establishes ATP-associated directional motion, not an ATP-per-turn yield, torque, universal camera sign or completed reverse-synthesis experiment. Proposed numerical settings may earn credit when explicitly qualified.
Correct the draft reference by explicitly requiring magnesium/cofactor and nucleotide speciation qualification; its generic reaction inventory is not a complete buffer recipe.
Reverse operation should generate new ATP repeatedly beyond measured initial available/bound pools. Three catalytic sites are not a universal total ATP-contamination bound.

Luciferase is an acceptable chemical readout when its consumption, recovery and time response are calibrated. An intensity slope is not generally synthesis flux; chromatographic detection is an alternative, not mandatory.
Label incorporation can reflect exchange. Pair isotope provenance with net-product/material balance; account for reporter consumption and sample removal as appropriate.
Empirical direction, mixed surface orientations, actual rotor turns and transmitted torque are distinct quantities. Do not replace any with the nominal actuator command.

Mechanical input can drive ATP synthesis uphill. Low initial ATP may aid sensitivity but does not prove positive chemical-energy storage; energetic efficiency needs both work and chemical free energy.

ATP per turn is a coupling yield, not energetic efficiency. Inactive fractions, orientation, incomplete entrainment and analytical recovery can reduce apparent yield without establishing loose molecular coupling.
Separate ADP and phosphate controls help discriminate intended synthesis from alternative ATP production. Inhibitor effects require assay and enzyme specificity validation.

Matching is retrospective and applies all five predeclared components. A partially correct historical direction is recorded even when the experimental design is flawed; no claim of prospective novelty or uncontaminated holdout is made.
